movie_updates.title: Anaconda
movie_updates.description: Anaconda is a comedy about two friends' (Paul Rudd, Jack Black) attempt to remake the 1997 cult classic, only to face attacks by a real giant anaconda. In addition to humans being snatched or devoured by giant snakes, the action includes gun threats, shootings, head-butting, a snake getting torn to pieces by a propellor, characters being knocked out, a wounded face slammed up against a window, and more. A character who's thought to be dead is used as a distraction, with a dead boar duct-taped to his head and a dead squirrel inserted into his mouth. Characters flirt, and there's dialogue related to cheating. Language includes a use of 'f--k', plus 's--t', 'a--hole', 'ass', 'bitch', 'goddamn', 'hell', 'Jesus', 'Christ', 'oh my God', 'piss', 'damn'.

movie_updates.title: The Great Flood
movie_updates.description: A mother wakes up in her apartment to her 5-year-old boy exclaiming that there's water everywhere outside. Before she knows it, the water level of her entire apartment complex is rising, and she and her son must fight to get to the roof before they are washed away. There's some gun violence, shootouts, and fighting. Characters get shot in the chest and head (impacts not shown) and die. Characters fight, wrestle, punch, kick, throw, hit, and choke other characters. A character strangles another character to death. A character is dragged by her hair. A character throws two people out of a high story window after breaking their arms. Many people get caught in huge flooding, struggle to swim, and drown. Dead bodies float along the water's surface and underwater. Huge waves crash into and through buildings and windows, taking people along, many dying in the process. A 5-year-old boy is handcuffed to a railing. People also shave the boy's head and take a circular saw to the boy's scalp (not shown).

movie_updates.title: Now You See Me: Now You Don't
movie_updates.description: Now You See Me: Now You Don't is the third installment in the popular heist franchise. It reunites the original four Horsemen—Danny (Jesse Eisenberg), Merritt (Woody Harrelson), Jack (Dave Franco), and Henley (Isla Fisher)—as well as their nemesis-turned-ally, Thaddeus (Morgan Freeman), and a few new faces, to right a wrong through teamwork and sleight of hand. The main characters are still Robin Hood-style vigilantes, putting themselves at risk to stage elaborately planned performances during which they shift the fortunes of greedy CEOs to those who are deserving. It's justice, but it's also a heist, and the characters lie and fight with authority figures to pull it off. Expect mild but exciting action violence, with pushing, punches, and heads getting hit with hard objects. A shooting has fatal consequences but no blood. The group also throws insults at each other faster than Jack throws playing cards, with some involving strong language like s--t,
a--hole, and d--k. A joke implies that a character took edibles, and characters hold alcoholic drinks but aren't shown actually drinking them. There's kissing and a suggestive joke.

movie_updates.title: Merv
movie_updates.description: Merv stars Zooey Deschanel and Charlie Cox and centers on a dog who is brokenhearted over his owners' breakup.

movie_updates.title: Influencers
movie_updates.description: Influencers is a sequel to Influencer about a queer lesbian serial killer, CW (Cassandra Naud), who targets social media and content creator celebrities. There are major moments of strong violence, killing, gore, blood, injury detail, self-harm, and suicide. A character slices her own neck with a kitchen knife, and the wound shows blood pouring out. A character pushes another down a deep well, and later the killer finds her alive but with a broken body, limbs awry, bloody, and bones coming out of places. A character bashes someone in the head with a heavy lamp, then uses the lamp cord to strangle the victim to death. A character is stabbed in the stomach with a knife, then stabbed many times in the chest, bleeds out, and dies. A character hacks into another character's neck and body with a butcher knife. A character experiences online harassment and abuse. Couples have sex, romantically kiss, and talk about intimate relationships. Bared breasts and bare buttocks are shown. A character films himself and two naked (no genitalia shown) people having sex. Characters are frequently shown in bathing suits, bikinis, underwear, and lingerie. Characters often drink alcohol, smoke cigarettes, and some snort cocaine.

movie_updates.title: Keeper
movie_updates.description: Keeper is director Osgood Perkins' creepy supernatural horror movie about a couple (Tatiana Maslany and Rossif Sutherland) that goes to a remote cabin in the woods for a romantic weekend, only to find something waiting. Violence includes scary images/moments, a body with its head almost cut off, a severed head, ghostly figures, guns used to threaten and shoot, shooting, flashes of screaming, bloody faces, and more. Characters kiss, and there's dialogue about an affair that uses the phrase side piece.

movie_updates.title: Predators
movie_updates.description: Predators is a documentary about the dangers of child predators, online safety, and the importance of protecting kids. The film doesn't show graphic violence, but children are harassed and targeted, there's an off-screen gunshot, and a character dies by suicide. Sexual content includes adult women in skimpy outfits used as decoys, some appearing underage. No explicit sexual acts are shown, but the film deals with sexual exploitation and predatory behavior.

movie_updates.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: The Last Straw
movie_updates.description: The film's central conflict is that Greg Heffley's father, Frank, is frustrated with Greg's wimpy behavior and lack of discipline. As a result, he threatens to send Greg to Spag Union Military Academy in the hopes it will toughen him up, to avoid this fate, Greg devises a plan: he must prove his worth by earning the Woodchipper Elite badge—a top honor from a local scouting group called the Woodchippers . Frank agrees to this deal, but a camping trip he must chaperone turns into a series of comedic disasters

movie_updates.title: The Housemaid
movie_updates.description: The Housemaid is director Paul Feig's female-centered psychological thriller based on Freida McFadden's bestselling book about a wealthy couple who hire domestic help. The premise seems to promise a plot that pits women (played by Amanda Seyfried and Sydney Sweeney) against each other, but it's actually much more than that. Expect steamy sex scenes with full nudity, including breasts and a solid view of a man's backside. Violence is also intense, with a brief rape scene , stabbing, pushing, punches, and kicks. Psychological torture that becomes bloody self-harm feels designed to make viewers cringe and squirm.

movie_updates.title: Avatar: Fire and Ash
movie_updates.description: Avatar: Fire and Ash is the third installment in director James Cameron's hit franchise. This time around, Jake (Sam Worthington) and Neytiri's (Zoe Saldaña) family faces off against a new foe, the Ash People raiders and their ruthless chief, Varang (Oona Chaplin), all while Pandora's escalating warfare brings forth more life-or-death obstacles. As in the previous installments, expect scenes of intense action violence, including explosions, armed combat, shots, and stabbings. Several prominent and supporting characters are injured or die, a couple of them during emotional moments.

movie_updates.title: Goodbye June
movie_updates.description: Goodbye June is an intense but moving family drama about a group of adult children who rush to their dying mother's bedside just a few weeks before Christmas. It's Kate Winslet's debut movie as director, based on a script by her son, Joe Anders. The titular character (Helen Mirren) collapses and is taken to the hospital, where doctors reveal that her cancer has spread, and she doesn't have long to live. Much of the film sees her in a hospital bed, hooked up to machines, and often in visible pain.

movie_updates.title: Silent Night, Deadly Night
movie_updates.description: Silent Night, Deadly Night—a remake of a 1984 holiday-themed slasher movie—is about a killer who dresses as Santa Claus (Rohan Campbell). Violence is very gory, with guns and shooting (sometimes fatally), bloody/decomposed corpses, and kids being hurt/in peril (beaten with a hockey stick, abducted, drugged, physically threatened). Characters are chopped up in various ways with an axel; there's a beheading, severed limbs, entrails, blood spatter, and much more. Couples flirt and kiss, and two people are seen after sex, naked under the covers (no sensitive body parts shown)

movie_updates.title: The Plague
movie_updates.description: The Plague is an intense coming-of-age drama that tells a Lord of the Flies-esque story about adolescent boys at a water polo summer camp. The film deals with self-esteem, anxiety, peer pressure, and other hot-button issues for teens. Violence include property destruction, fighting, and self-harm that crosses the line into body horror, such as digging fingernails into skin until bleeding, skin pricking, and a graphic, bloody scene of a boy cutting his own fingers off with scissors. The boys characters also talk about fairly explicit sexual situations, drink alcohol, and smoke drugs.

movie_updates.title: The Night My Dad Saved Christmas 2
movie_updates.description: The Night My Dad Saved Christmas 2 is a Spanish-language holiday comedy about a father and son who team up to rescue Santa from a greedy toy company trying to take over Christmas. Violence stays mostly slapstick but includes threats and weapons that may feel intense for younger kids. Kids fire Nerf-style guns, adults break into buildings, and characters lock Santa in a box. Villains point a gun at Santa and fire a tranquilizer dart. Two Santas duel with oversized candy canes. A character drinks alcohol, and others comment on the smell; Santa drinks maple liquor. Mild romantic content includes a crush and a cheek kiss. On the positive side, the story emphasizes family bonds, teamwork, and choosing kindness over greed.
